To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the weight space of a MLP is highly complex and non linear, (b) the weight space is not uniform in terms of convergence and generalization capabilities of the MLP, (c) there exist regions in the weight space that are not reachable by any gradient based training algorithm and (d) the weight space contains regions that lead to fast convergence to local minima with good generalization performance and other regions that lead to slow convergence or divergence.

the MLPs weight space is not a continuous space, but a set of disjoint regions, that the initial values of weights are very critical and that there is a region of the weight space where the MLPs are able to solve a given problem, and there is a region where the MLPs cannot learn a given problem at all.

the initial weight space in complex real world tasks is not a uniform space and that it can be partitioned in regions with different convergence and generalization capabilities, which is a very important result that can be used to improve the initialization of the weights in MLPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the analysis of the weight space in MLP, and (ii) the use of SOM for this analysis, (iii) the application of the above analysis to the initialization problem of MLPs, and (iv) the extension of previous results on MLP initialization in the literature.
the analysis of the initial weight space of the MLPs and with the investigation of the relationship of this space with the convergence and generalization capability.

the following issues: - The application of data mining techniques to the analysis of the MLP's weight space - The analysis of the initial weight space of MLPs in complex real world tasks, in terms of convergence and generalization - The study of the effect of the initialization procedure on the convergence and generalization properties of MLPs - The study of MLP's weight space in order to identify regions of the weight space that correspond to successful and unsuccessful solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initial weight space is a complex space, where the regions with good generalization capability are not isolated and can be reached from any point in the initial weight space.
the initial weight space of MLPs is a complex multidimensional hyperspace with a lot of local minima, a lot of local maxima and a few global minima.

the initial weight space of MLPs is highly nonuniform, with many regions of poor generalization and slow convergence, and some regions where the generalization is good and convergence fast, even with simple gradient-based training procedures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a complete analysis on the MLP initial weight space is possible, even in the case that the problem to be solved is complex.
there are regions in the weight space where MLP is able to converge to a solution with fast convergence rate and good generalization performance.

a complete analysis, based on SOM algorithm, of the weight space of MLPs is possible even in complex real world problems and that the results of such analysis are very important in order to improve the initialization procedures of MLP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the weight space of MLP is highly structured and that this structure can be used to guide MLP initialization procedures to regions of better convergence and/or generalization.
the weight space of MLPs solving complex real world tasks is very complex and the use of data mining tools is a promising approach to reveal its structure.
MLPs have a very rich initial weight space, which is very important to be studied in order to design more efficient MLP training procedures.
